correctness.rationale: Given Branco–Colaço–Ojeda Theorem 15 canonical Apéry vectors for generalized repunits, the residue-height formula W(T)=m c(T)+2T follows, as checked against independently computed Dijkstra Apéry minima. The ±1 Mersenne coin lemma follows from odd parity and splitting a large coin into two half-size coins. The nonstandard shift identity c(h+t)=1+c(t+1) is proved by binary power splitting, with n>=3 and t=0..h-2 boundaries explicit. Neighbor threshold inequalities show one isolated gap at each t and a second iff c(t+1)-c(t)=1; telescoping gives h/2 increasing steps and |I|=3*2^(n-2)-1. Independently computed complete gap sets and Apéry minima for n=2..7. Finite confirmation is not an all-n proof.
